newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Pope urges U.N. chief to work for Zaire cease-fire.
newsitem.headline: Pope urges U.N. chief to work for Zaire cease-fire.

text.p: Pope John Paul II has urged Secretary-General Kofi Annan to do everything possible to obtain a ceasefire in Zaire, where government troops and rebels have been battling since last October.

"The fighting which is unfolding in the eastern part of the country is once again plunging the people there into a human drama before which the leaders of the nations cannot remain unfeeling," the pontiff said in a letter handed to Annan on Tuesday by the Holy See's U.N. observer, Archbishop Renato Martino.
The pope asked for his letter, dated March 3, to be brought to the attention of the Security Council.

"I cannot remain indifferent to the situation of these my brothers and sisters within humanity and I encourage you in every effort being employed, both on the ground and at the international level, to secure an immediate ceasefire," the letter said.

A special envoy representing both the United Nations and the Organisation of African Unity, Mohamed Sahnoun, is trying to implement a five-point peace plan whose first objective is a ceasefire. But the rebels, who are within a few miles (km) of the key town of Kisangani, have not agreed to halt their advance.

Alluding to fears about the breakup of the sprawling African country, the pope said it was of prime importance that, "in Zaire, as elsewhere, the principle of respect for territorial integrity be put into operation in an absolute manner, if you do not wish to open the door to every kind of excess."

He also called for the return home "in security and with dignity" of Rwandan refugees now in Zaire, saying this would be possible only through the collaboration of the international community and the peaceful involvement of African countries.
He said an equitable solution to all the problems affecting the people of the Great Lakes region would be easier if the "process of democratization begun in Zaire is completed."

All people of goodwill must be encouraged to create favourable conditions for a national dialogue involving all ethnic and political groupings, the pope said, adding that the Catholic Church was already playing its part.
